## Summary

Fixed the root cause in `/opt/veridian/scripts/supervisor-entrypoint.sh`: the tier1 merge block used `gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch`'s combined exit code as the sole success signal, so a real merge (API-confirmed) plus a failed local `--delete-branch` step (due to the sibling worktree conflict) was misreported as a failed merge.

**Fix**: split into `gh pr merge --merge` (own exit code no longer trusted alone) + a separate best-effort `gh api -X DELETE .../git/refs/heads/$BRANCH` for branch cleanup. Checkpoint success/failure is now gated purely on a fresh `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt` call.

**Evidence produced**:
- `tests/supervisor_merge_detection_test.sh` — extracts the real merge block from the live script (no reimplementation) and proves 3 scenarios pass against the fix, while 2 of them correctly fail when run against the reconstructed pre-fix logic.
- Retroactive read-only audit of all 12 merged + 2 open PRs on claude-control — no 4th unnoticed false-blocked instance found beyond the known #10/#13/#14.
- `ai-os/patches/supervisor-entrypoint-merge-report-fix-2026-07-24.diff` added to the repo's existing patch-archive convention.

**Real-world proof**: this task's own PR ([#15](https://github.com/FChecklist/claude-control/pull/15)) was pushed, then routed through the actual live `veridian-supervisor@` systemd service (real AI review, real tier1 auto-merge). Confirmed via `gh pr view`: `state=MERGED`, real `mergeCommit`, and the task's own checkpoint correctly reads `completed`, not `blocked` — the exact failure mode is fixed end-to-end, not just reviewed for correctness.
